title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 121
paragraphs: The lesser number of those who tell the tale, however, say that Oroetes sent a herald to Samos to ask for something—what it was is not mentioned—and Polycrates happened to be lying down in the men's chamber of his palace, with Anacreon of Teos present beside him. Somehow—whether by design, because he thought little of Oroetes' business, or by some chance occurrence—the envoy of Oroetes came into his presence and spoke with him, and Polycrates, who happened to be turned towards the wall, neither turned round at all nor gave any answer.
